close_reason: Landed in commit 989c678 (workspace AGENTS.md). Per ratified option (c): kept the HashMap<String, bool> set-as-map idiom as-is across the workspace; the breaking-API cost of migrating ~30 crates to HashSet<String> + serde adapter is too high for a defensive-typing improvement that the wire format already permits. New workspace AGENTS.md section 'Set-as-map idiom on the wire stays as HashMap<String, bool>' documents the policy with three numbered reasons (cross-crate breaking-change cost, wire-shape mirror posture, low defensive cost) and an explicit future-work escape hatch (jmap-types serde adapter driven by jmap-mail-types canonical-template) so the decision is reversible if a downstream consumer accumulates evidence of real bugs. Per-crate rustdoc / Gotchas not duplicated.
description:
RFC 9553 uses the set-as-map idiom for several fields where the value is
always 'true' and the key carries the meaning: 'contexts' on most types, and
'features' on Phone. Per RFC 9553 §1.5.1, the value must be the literal
true; the false value is not defined.

The crate types these fields as Option<HashMap<String, bool>>:

- Nickname.contexts:181, Pronouns.contexts:304, EmailAddress.contexts:364,
  OnlineService.contexts:410, Phone.contexts:450, LanguagePref.contexts:484,
  Calendar.contexts:529, SchedulingAddress.contexts:563, Address.contexts:619,
  CryptoKey.contexts:709, Directory.contexts:757, Link.contexts:812,
  Media.contexts:860, Organization.contexts:224 — all use Option<HashMap<String, bool>>.
- Phone.features:446 — same idiom.
- Relation.relation:1145 — same idiom.

A caller can construct .contexts = Some(HashMap::from([("work".into(), false)]))
and serialize a wire-invalid object that no spec-conformant peer should
process. Deserialize accepts it without complaint.

The set semantics are better expressed by HashSet<String>. Serializing a
HashSet to a {key: true} JSON map is a 10-line serde adapter. Deserializing
from a {key: true} JSON map back to HashSet ignores any value that is not
'true' (or rejects it as invalid).

Cost of the change is breaking for any caller currently building these fields
as HashMap<String, bool>. Benefit is permanent: no way to construct an invalid
contexts field; iteration is HashSet semantics; the field is also smaller
in memory.

Status-quo defense: 'serde_json round-trips it' — true, but the type fails to
model the spec invariant, and downstream code that calls .iter() and pattern
matches on values handles the value when it should match on the key alone.
title: contexts/features HashMap<String, bool> set-as-map idiom — false values permitted but nonsensical
